name: Sunrise at Shiloh Mesa
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: Greccio Housing built Sunrise at Shiloh Mesa, a 50-unit, four-story apartment building for seniors 62 and older at 30% to 50% AMI, on about an acre donated by Woodmen Valley Chapel's Center for Strategic Ministry in northeast Colorado Springs. It won $1,377,143 a year in federal 9% credit and $700,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2024 Round One, broke ground in July 2025 and held its grand opening in August 2026.
why_it_matters: It is a finished example of church land donated for deeply affordable senior housing: the free site kept debt low enough to put every unit at or below 50% AMI, and church volunteers supply transportation and services.

background.text: Land deal: the Center for Strategic Ministry, Woodmen Valley Chapel's outreach arm, set aside about an acre of its master-planned Shiloh Mesa holdings and agreed in 2021 to donate it to Greccio for senior housing; the site had been planned as a parking lot.

Three applications: the project first applied in CHFA's 2022 Round One and again in 2023 Round One before winning in 2024. The 2022 plan had 12 units at 30%, 18 at 40% and 20 at 50% AMI; the 2023 and 2024 applications shifted to 15, 12 and 23. Between rounds Greccio added a transportation plan and an expanded church service agreement, including emergency rent help.

Approvals: density is set by the neighborhood PUD and the applicant said only administrative site plan approval was needed. Neighbor input led to the stepped three-to-four-story north end so the building does not block Pikes Peak views or overlook backyards.

Cost savings cited by the applicant: free land, low Colorado Springs tap fees, utility infrastructure offsets, the city's affordable housing materials tax abatement and a regional stormwater system that avoids on-site detention.

Services: church volunteers provide transportation (a shuttle until public bus service reaches the Woodmen Road corridor), activities, food pantry access and welcome support; Greccio adds its resident resources programs. The 2021 plan targeted an opening in spring 2024.

Market: the application's study found no vacancies and waitlists at surveyed tax credit properties, a two-month lease-up and a 15.9% overall capture rate; Greccio's Atrium at Austin Bluffs senior property had a waitlist of more than 400 seniors in 2025.
The plan grew from the 2021 concept of a three-story building with 45 to 50 units to the four-story, 50-unit building in the 2024 application.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the address as 8292 Woodman Valley View, the application narrative gives 8292 E. Woodmen Valley Road, and the grand opening notice gives 7727 Mulberry Wood Drive.

CHFA's award description gives 15 units at 30% AMI, 12 at 40% and 23 at 50%, while the Gazette's 2025 groundbreaking story gives 12 at 30%, 18 at 40% and 20 at 50%, which matches the 2022 application.
